# React Native Sync Provider

> Cross-platform React Native Nitro Module for offline-first HTTP sync on Android and iOS: a native, persistent request queue with a declarative retry policy and OS-scheduled background dispatch.

## Package

- npm: @gabriel-sisjr/react-native-sync-provider
- Repository: https://github.com/gabriel-sisjr/react-native-sync-provider
- Documentation: https://gabriel-sisjr.github.io/react-native-sync-provider/
- Full reference for tools: /llms-full.txt

## Overview

A cross-platform React Native library for offline-first HTTP sync built on Nitro Modules, for the New Architecture. Persists outbound requests on the native side, retries them on a persisted backoff, and can dispatch them in OS-scheduled background windows while the app is not running, on both Android and iOS. Android uses Room, OkHttp and WorkManager; iOS uses Core Data, URLSession and BGTaskScheduler. Features include a queue that survives a force-quit and a reboot, linear, exponential or Fibonacci backoff with jitter, a dead-letter queue for requests that fail permanently, a network-quality level on every connection snapshot with an opt-in quality gate and health check, configuration persisted for background workers with `defaultHeaders` encrypted at rest, priority lanes, nine React hooks, and typed events and errors.

## Requirements

- React Native >= 0.74.0, with the New Architecture enabled
- React >= 18.2.0
- react-native-nitro-modules ^0.35.8 (0.35.8 or later, below 0.36)
- Optional peer: @react-native-community/netinfo >= 11.0.0
- Optional peer: react-native-mmkv >= 3.0.0
- Android: minSdk 24. The library reads `minSdkVersion`, `compileSdkVersion`, `targetSdkVersion` and `kotlinVersion` from the app's `ext` block, defaulting to 24, 36, 36 and Kotlin 2.0.21, and has a matching KSP version for Kotlin 2.0.21 to 2.2.21
- iOS: 15.0+
- Expo: development build only. There is no config plugin, so apply the iOS setup to the native project. With Continuous Native Generation, `expo prebuild` regenerates `ios/`: set `UIBackgroundModes` and `BGTaskSchedulerPermittedIdentifiers` through `ios.infoPlist`, and add the `AppDelegate` forwarding with a config plugin; see /docs/troubleshooting#faq

## Facts that are easy to get wrong

- `enqueue` stores an item. It does not dispatch it, under any strategy. A flush does, from `useAutoSync`, `flush()`, `drainUntilEmpty()` or an OS background window. After `resumeSync()`, and on iOS also after a failed health check, the retry timer flushes items with no cooldown too, unless the strategy is `MANUAL`. `replayDeadLetter()` does not flush either.
- `AUTOMATIC` means the engine retries failed items on its own: an in-process timer, plus the Android retry kick while background sync is enabled. Enqueueing does not trigger a native flush, and a reconnect alone does not either: only a retry wake the timer held while offline runs then.
- `MANUAL` stops the engine from scheduling flushes, not `useAutoSync`: the hook never reads the strategy. Pass `enabled: false` for a manual flow.
- Each cycle dispatches one batch of eligible items, up to `batchSize` (default 25). Use `drainUntilEmpty()` to loop.
- `flush()` checks connectivity only through `minNetworkQuality`. Unset, a flush while offline can spend retry attempts and move valid items to the dead-letter queue. `minNetworkQuality: 'POOR'` blocks only `OFFLINE`. `useAutoSync`'s interval and foreground flushes, the native retry timer and `drainUntilEmpty()` do not flush while `DISCONNECTED`.
- Per-item failures never reject. Read them from `ITEM_FAILED` events. A permanent failure moves the item to the dead-letter queue: `ITEM_FAILED`, then `ITEM_DEAD_LETTERED`. Nothing prunes that queue: replay or discard each dead letter.
- A cycle the quality gate or the health check skips runs nothing: `SYNC_FAILED` with `NETWORK_QUALITY_TOO_LOW` or `HEALTH_CHECK_FAILED`, no `SYNC_STARTED`, no item change, no history row, and a 0/0 result.
- Without `healthCheckUrl`, `networkQuality` never reaches `EXCELLENT`, so `minNetworkQuality: 'EXCELLENT'` blocks every flush. Compare levels by their index in `Object.values(NetworkQuality)`, never as strings.
- `CONNECTION_CHANGED` carries only `connectionStatus`, also when only `networkQuality` changed, and is never emitted for the starting state. Read `getConnectionStatus()` at start and on each event, or use `useConnection()`.
- Native error codes do not reach JS through a rejection. A full queue rejects with `INVALID_PAYLOAD` and no `validationErrors`, not `QUEUE_FULL`.
- `configureSync` replaces the whole configuration and persists it. Omitting `defaultHeaders` deletes the stored copy. `getSyncConfig()` can come back without the headers, so set them yourself before passing its result back.
- `clearQueue()` also deletes every dead letter, and `removeItem(id)` removes the dead letter with that id when no queued item has it.
- Delivery is at least once. The native ULID is not sent with the request: send an `Idempotency-Key` in `headers`, built with `generateId()` before `enqueue`.
- `ConnectionType` `BLUETOOTH` and `VPN` are reported by Android only. iOS reports `WIFI`, `CELLULAR`, `ETHERNET`, `OTHER`, `NONE` or `UNKNOWN`.
- iOS: the library registers its BGTask handlers itself. Do not call `BGTaskScheduler.shared.register` for its identifiers.

## Public API

### Queue Functions
- `enqueue(item)` — Persist one request. Returns the assigned ULID. Does not dispatch.
- `enqueueBatch(items)` — Persist several atomically. Returns ULIDs in input order. Invalid input throws one `INVALID_PAYLOAD` that lists every issue.
- `removeItem(id)` — Remove one item, pending or in flight, or else the dead letter with that id. Returns whether a row was removed. Does not cancel a request in flight.
- `clearQueue()` — Remove every item, in any status, and every dead letter. Emits one `QUEUE_CLEARED`.
- `getQueueSize()` — `PENDING` items, cooling ones included. In-flight items and dead letters are not counted.
- `getPendingItems()` — `PENDING` items in dispatch order, cooling ones included.

### Dead-Letter Functions
- `listDeadLetter()` — Every dead letter, oldest first: by `deadLetteredAt`, then `id`.
- `replayDeadLetter(id)` — Put a dead letter back as `PENDING` under the same id, with `attempts: 0`. Emits `ITEM_ENQUEUED`. Does not flush.
- `discardDeadLetter(id)` — Delete a dead letter. Emits `ITEM_REMOVED` when a row was deleted.

### Sync Functions
- `flush()` — Run one cycle. Returns `SyncResult`. Per-item failures never reject.
- `drainUntilEmpty(options?)` — Flush until empty or a bound stops it. Returns `DrainResult`. One drain per process.
- `cancelDrain()` — Hard stop for a running drain. A no-op when none runs.
- `pauseSync()` — Pause until `resumeSync()` or the next launch. Persisted, so background workers stay inert.
- `resumeSync()` — Resume. Dispatches pending items unless the strategy is `MANUAL`.
- `isSyncing()` — `true` while a cycle is running.

### Configuration Functions
- `configureSync(options)` — Replace and persist the active `SyncOptions`. Validates `minNetworkQuality`, `healthCheckUrl`, `healthCheckTtlMs` and `healthCheckBackoffMs` in JS.
- `getSyncConfig()` — Read the active `SyncOptions`. Those four options appear only when they were set.

### History Functions
- `getLastSyncResult()` — Most recent persisted `SyncResult`, or `undefined`.
- `getSyncHistory(limit?)` — Persisted results, most recent first. No limit when omitted.
- `clearSyncHistory()` — Drop persisted history. The queue is untouched.

### Connection Functions
- `getConnectionStatus()` — Current `ConnectionState` snapshot, `networkQuality` included.

### Background Sync Functions
- `enableBackgroundSync(options)` — Schedule OS background work: WorkManager on Android, BGTaskScheduler on iOS.
- `disableBackgroundSync()` — Cancel it, including the Android retry kick.
- `isBackgroundSyncEnabled()` — Reports intent, not OS state.

### Event Listeners
- `addSyncEventListener(callback)` — Subscribe to the `sync-event` channel. Returns a subscription id.
- `removeSyncEventListener(subscriptionId)` — Unsubscribe.
- `SYNC_EVENT_CHANNEL` — The channel name, `'sync-event'`.

### Utilities
- `generateId()` — UUID v4 backed by `Math.random`, not cryptographically secure. For `Idempotency-Key` headers.
- `isNativeModuleAvailable()` — `true` when the native module resolves.

### React Hooks
- `useConnection()` — `{ status, type, isOnline, isMetered, networkQuality }`.
- `useSyncQueue()` — `{ size, items, isLoading, error, enqueue, enqueueBatch, removeItem, clearQueue, refresh }`.
- `useSyncStatus()` — `{ isSyncing, isPaused, progress, lastResult, error, flush, pause, resume }`.
- `useOfflineQueue()` — `{ connection, size, items, isSyncing, isWaitingForConnection, error, enqueue, flush }`.
- `useSyncEvents({ onEvent, types?, enabled? })` — Subscribe with auto-cleanup.
- `useSyncConfig()` — `{ config, isLoading, error, setConfig, refresh }`.
- `useAutoSync({ enabled?, intervalMs?, flushOnReconnect?, flushOnMetered?, flushOnAppForeground? })` — Flush on an interval, on reconnect and on foreground. The interval and foreground flushes skip while `DISCONNECTED`. Inert unless `enabled` is `true`.
- `useSyncSnapshot()` — Read-only aggregate: `{ connection, size, items, isSyncing, isPaused, progress, lastResult, isWaitingForConnection, error, networkQuality?, deadLetter? }`.
- `useSyncContext()` — `{ config, hasProvider }`.

### Context
- `SyncProvider` — Optional provider. Applies `configureSync` on mount and on every change to `options`, and `enableBackgroundSync` when `backgroundSync` is passed. Every hook works without it.
- `SyncProviderContext` — The context object. Default value `{ config: undefined, hasProvider: false }`.

### Enums
- `SyncStrategy` — AUTOMATIC, MANUAL, OPPORTUNISTIC (reserved; behaves like AUTOMATIC)
- `SyncPriority` — HIGH, NORMAL, LOW
- `BackoffStrategy` — LINEAR, EXPONENTIAL, FIBONACCI
- `HttpMethod` — GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE
- `NetworkQuality` — OFFLINE, POOR, MODERATE, GOOD, EXCELLENT (worst to best)
- `SyncEventType` (16) — ITEM_ENQUEUED, ITEM_REMOVED, SYNC_STARTED, SYNC_PROGRESS, SYNC_SUCCEEDED, SYNC_FAILED, ITEM_SUCCEEDED, ITEM_FAILED, ITEM_RETRYING, QUEUE_CLEARED, CONNECTION_CHANGED, PAUSED, RESUMED, BACKGROUND_SYNC_STARTED, BACKGROUND_SYNC_COMPLETED, ITEM_DEAD_LETTERED
- `ConnectionStatus` — CONNECTED, DISCONNECTED, METERED, UNKNOWN
- `ConnectionType` — WIFI, CELLULAR, ETHERNET, BLUETOOTH (Android only), VPN (Android only), OTHER, NONE, UNKNOWN
- `SyncErrorCode` (15) — NETWORK_ERROR, SERVER_ERROR, INVALID_PAYLOAD, QUEUE_FULL, NATIVE_MODULE_UNAVAILABLE, BACKGROUND_TASK_REGISTRATION_FAILED, INVALID_URL, UNAUTHORIZED, TIMEOUT, MAX_ATTEMPTS_EXCEEDED, DUPLICATE_ITEM, DRAIN_ALREADY_ACTIVE, NETWORK_QUALITY_TOO_LOW, HEALTH_CHECK_FAILED, DEAD_LETTERED

### Key Types
- `SyncItemInput` — What you enqueue: `{ method, url, headers?, body?, contentType?, priority?, metadata? }`
- `SyncItem` — `SyncItemInput` + `{ id, createdAt, attempts, nextRetryAt }`
- `SyncDeadLetterItem` — A permanently failed request: the `SyncItem` fields except `nextRetryAt`, plus `{ lastAttemptAt, lastErrorCode, lastErrorMessage?, deadLetteredAt }`
- `SyncOptions` — `{ strategy, retryPolicy, batchSize?, requestTimeoutMs?, maxQueueSize?, persistQueue?, defaultHeaders?, minNetworkQuality?, healthCheckUrl?, healthCheckTtlMs?, healthCheckBackoffMs? }`
- `RetryPolicy` — `{ maxAttempts, backoff, baseDelayMs, maxDelayMs, jitter, retryOnStatusCodes }`
- `SyncResult` — `{ startedAt, finishedAt, successCount, failureCount, succeededIds, failedIds, errors }`. The ids and `errors` are always empty on iOS
- `DrainOptions` — `{ maxIterations?, timeoutMs?, delayBetweenCyclesMs? }`
- `DrainResult` — `{ iterations, itemsDispatched, queueRemaining, stoppedReason }`, with `stoppedReason` one of `'EMPTY' | 'MAX_ITERATIONS' | 'TIMEOUT' | 'CANCELLED'`
- `BackgroundSyncOptions` — `{ minimumIntervalMs, requiresCharging?, requiresUnmeteredNetwork?, requiresDeviceIdle?, foregroundOnly?, taskIdentifier? }`
- `ConnectionState` — `{ status, type, networkQuality, isInternetReachable?, isExpensive? }`
- `SyncEvent` — Flat object: `{ type, timestamp, itemId?, progress?, errorCode?, statusCode?, attempt?, connectionStatus?, metadata? }`
- `SyncError` — `Error` subclass with `.code`, `.cause?` and `.validationErrors?`
- `ValidationIssue` — `{ field, reason, value?, itemIndex? }`
